item.question: A baker bakes 14 loaves every day except Sunday. Write expressions for the loaves in 6 weeks in two ways and find the value.
steps: Baking days in a week: 7 − 1 = 6. In 6 weeks: (7 − 1) × 6 = 36 days.
Other way: all days 7 × 6 × 14 = 588, take away the shut days 1 × 6 × 14 = 84, and 588 − 84 = 504.
Both expressions give 504 loaves.
item.text:
Worked example: A baker bakes 14 loaves every day except Sunday. Write expressions for the loaves in 6 weeks in two ways and find the value.
1. Baking days in a week: 7 − 1 = 6. In 6 weeks: (7 − 1) × 6 = 36 days.
2. Loaves: (7 − 1) × 6 × 14 = 36 × 14 = 504.
3. Other way: all days 7 × 6 × 14 = 588, take away the shut days 1 × 6 × 14 = 84, and 588 − 84 = 504.
4. Both expressions give 504 loaves.
Answer: (7 − 1) × 6 × 14 = 7 × 6 × 14 − 1 × 6 × 14 = 504 loaves

item.question: Read the situations given below. Write appropriate expressions for each of them and find their values. (a) The district market in Begur operates on all seven days of a week. In how many days will the snail get the treat?
steps_tex: $(a)$: Each day they supply $9 + 11\text{ kg}$, for $7$ days: $7 \times (9 + 11) = 7 \times 20 = 140\text{ kg}$.

$(c)$: Each full day the snail gains $3 - 2 = 1\text{ cm}$, so after $7$ days it is at $7\text{ cm}$. On the $8\text{th}$ day it climbs $3\text{ cm}$ to reach $10\text{ cm}$ before the night: $7 \times (3 - 2) + 3 = 10$. So $8$ days.
steps: (a) Each day they supply 9 + 11 kg, for 7 days: 7 × (9 + 11) = 7 × 20 = 140 kg.
(c) Each full day the snail gains 3 − 2 = 1 cm, so after 7 days it is at 7 cm. On the 8th day it climbs 3 cm to reach 10 cm before the night: 7 × (3 − 2) + 3 = 10. So 8 days.
item.text:
$1$. $(a)$: Each day they supply $9 + 11\text{ kg}$, for $7$ days: $7 \times (9 + 11) = 7 \times 20 = 140\text{ kg}$.
$2$. $(b)$: Each month she saves $20000 - (5000 + 5000 + 2000) = 8000$. In $12$ months: $12 \times 20000 - 12 \times (5000 + 5000 + 2000) = 240000 - 144000 =$ ₹$96000$.
$3$. $(c)$: Each full day the snail gains $3 - 2 = 1\text{ cm}$, so after $7$ days it is at $7\text{ cm}$. On the $8\text{th}$ day it climbs $3\text{ cm}$ to reach $10\text{ cm}$ before the night: $7 \times (3 - 2) + 3 = 10$. So $8$ days.
Answer: $(a)$: $7 \times (9 + 11) = 140\text{ kg} (b)$: ₹$96000$; $(c)$: $8$ days

item.text:
Worked example: Using three 3s, the four operations and brackets, find expressions for 0, 2, 4, 6, 9 and 12.
1. 0: 3 × (3 − 3) = 0.
2. 2: (3 + 3) ÷ 3 = 2.
3. 4: 3 + 3 ÷ 3 = 3 + 1 = 4.
4. 6: 3 × 3 − 3 = 9 − 3 = 6.
5. 9: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9.
6. 12: 3 × 3 + 3 = 9 + 3 = 12.
Answer: 0, 2, 4, 6, 9 and 12 are all reachable
